seoTitle: How to Set Up Payment Options in Wix (Accept Payments)
metaDescription: Open Wix's Accept Payments settings and connect PayPal, manual offline payments, or Wix's own processor, including the paid-plan requirement that applies to all three, not just Wix Payments.
intro: Getting paid on a Wix site starts in one place: the Accept Payments settings hub, tucked inside Finance & payments. What you'll actually see there depends on your plan and region, and the plan requirement reaches further than most people expect: Wix requires a plan that supports payments before any method works, including PayPal and Manual Payments, not just its own native processor. This guide walks through that settings hub as it really appears, including the PayPal and manual payment setup flows, so you know exactly what to expect before you commit to a plan.
prerequisites: A Wix site on a plan that supports payments — PayPal and Manual Payments need this too, not only Wix's native processor
costNote: None of the three methods are free to set up: even PayPal and Manual Payments require the site to be on a paid plan that supports payments, and PayPal adds its own per-transaction fee on top. Manual Payments is the only one with no processing fee, but it also has no automated refund tool.

steps.heading: Open your Wix dashboard
steps.body: Log into your Wix account and land on the site's Home dashboard. The left sidebar is where every settings area lives, including Getting Paid, a few rows below Home. If your site is on the Free plan, dashboard prompts nudge you toward a paid tier throughout, and payments are one of the reasons why: accepting money through any method needs a plan upgrade first, which the next step covers.

image.caption: The Wix site dashboard home screen, with Getting Paid and other finance-related sections listed in the left sidebar.

steps.heading: Go to Settings and open Accept Payments
steps.body: Click into Settings, then find the Finance & payments group near the top. Accept payments is the first item listed, described plainly as "Choose the way you get paid by customers." This is the entry point for every payment method Wix supports on your site, whether that's Wix's own processor, PayPal, or a manual offline option.

image.caption: The Settings page's Finance & payments section, with Accept payments as the first option and Getting paid, Receipts, and Tax beneath it.

steps.heading: Know the plan requirement before you pick a method
steps.body: Wix's own support documentation is specific here: your site needs a plan that supports payments before any method works, not only Wix's native processor. That rules out the Free plan for PayPal and Manual Payments too, which is easy to miss since both get described as the lighter-weight alternatives to upgrading. Wix Payments, the native processor for cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay, has the added requirement of running on a plan and region where Wix itself supports it. Check the Accept Payments page on your own site before assuming a method is available: it shows Connect for what you can use and Upgrade for what you can't.

steps.heading: Connect PayPal
steps.body: PayPal is one of the gateways available without Wix's native processor, though it still needs the site on a plan that supports payments. The Connect PayPal screen walks through three steps: enter your PayPal account email, click Connect, then log in on PayPal's site to finish linking the two accounts. Wix displays PayPal's fee structure on the same page and flags a real constraint: the currency your website uses has to match the currency on your PayPal account, or transactions won't process.

image.caption: The Connect PayPal setup screen, listing the three connection steps and PayPal's transaction fees alongside a currency-matching warning.

steps.heading: Set up Manual Payments for offline orders
steps.body: Manual Payments covers anything collected outside checkout itself: cash on delivery, a bank transfer, an in-person handoff. Pick a payment type from the dropdown, such as offline payment or cash on delivery, then write the instructions customers see at checkout explaining how to actually pay you. There's no processing fee, but Wix is explicit that a manual payment can't be refunded, deleted, or have its status changed from the Payments tab once it's marked Paid; any correction happens directly with the customer instead.

image.caption: The Connect Manual Payments screen, where you choose an offline payment type and write the instructions customers see at checkout.

steps.heading: Choose the method that fits your business
steps.body: Wix Payments is the only option that lets customers pay with cards directly at checkout without redirecting to PayPal, and it tends to convert better for that reason, but it's the one gated behind both a paid plan and regional availability. PayPal is the fastest to set up if your customers already trust it, at the cost of PayPal's own transaction fee on top of whatever Wix charges. Manual Payments has no fees at all but pushes the collection, and any refund, back onto you and the customer, outside Wix's own tools. For more than a handful of orders, budget for whichever plan unlocks Wix Payments; for early testing or low volume, PayPal or Manual Payments get you started without that commitment.

troubleshooting.problem: Accept Payments only shows Upgrade next to every method
troubleshooting.cause: The site is on the Free plan, which can't accept payments through any method, including PayPal and Manual Payments.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade to a plan that supports payments; which specific plan qualifies depends on your region, shown on the Accept Payments page itself.

troubleshooting.problem: PayPal fails to connect or process a payment after login
troubleshooting.cause: The currency set on the Wix site doesn't match the currency on the PayPal account.
troubleshooting.fix: Match the two currencies, either by changing the site's currency or connecting a PayPal account set to the same one.

troubleshooting.problem: A manual payment needs to be refunded
troubleshooting.cause: Wix's Payments tab has no refund, delete, or status-change tool for manual payments once they're marked Paid.
troubleshooting.fix: Refund the customer directly outside Wix, then keep your own record of it, since Wix won't reflect it.

faq.question: Do I need a paid Wix plan to accept payments?
faq.answer: Yes, for every method. Wix's support documentation states that accepting payments through PayPal or Manual Payments needs a plan that supports payments, the same as Wix's own processor. The Free plan can't take payments at all.

faq.question: Does PayPal charge extra fees on top of Wix?
faq.answer: Yes. PayPal's transaction fees appear directly on the Connect PayPal setup screen, and Wix doesn't add a separate fee on top of them.

faq.question: What is Manual Payments for?
faq.answer: It lets customers pay you outside the normal checkout flow, using instructions you write yourself, and it carries no processing fee. It also can't be refunded through Wix's Payments tab once marked Paid.

faq.question: Why does my PayPal connection fail even after I log in?
faq.answer: The most common cause is a currency mismatch. The currency set on your Wix website has to match the currency on your PayPal account for transactions to process correctly.

faq.question: Can I refund a manual payment through Wix?
faq.answer: No. Once a manual payment is marked Paid, Wix's Payments tab can't refund it, delete it, or change its status. Any refund has to be handled directly with the customer.
